notes: requirements.toml applies to every Codex session on the machine, and users can't override it. It is one file: merge by hand if your organization already has one.
Managed hooks skip the /hooks trust review, and [features] hooks = true turns hooks on where a user turned them off. If selfhost agents configure also added hooks to ~/.codex, Codex runs both.
Codex's docs say rules decide which commands run outside the sandbox. Whether forbidden also stops a command Codex runs inside the sandbox needs a real Codex session to confirm.
Codex hooks can't ask yet: an ask from the selfhost hook lets the call run.

rules.detail: Codex splits a shell script into commands only when it is plain words joined by &&, ||, ; or |, so commands with redirections, $(...) or variables are missed. The selfhost hook checks the rest.

Codex splits a shell script into commands only when it is plain words joined by &&, ||, ; or |, so commands with redirections, $(...) or variables are missed; a prefix rule matches whole words, so a last word that only starts with --hard is missed. The selfhost hook checks the rest.
Prefix rules match from a command's first word, and rm -rf has no ^ before it. The selfhost hook checks it.
Codex prefix rules match literal words, and the regular expression uses quantifier .*. The selfhost hook checks it.
Codex reports file paths only for apply_patch edits, and requirements.toml can deny reads ([permissions.filesystem] deny_read) but not edits. The selfhost hook checks it.
